verses.zh: 那时，耶稣在安息日从麦地经过。他的门徒饿了，就掐起麦穗来吃。
verses.en: At that time Jesus went through the grain fields on a Sabbath. His[NOTE:1] disciples were hungry, and they began to pick heads of wheat[NOTE:2] and eat them.
notes: Here δέ (de) has not been translated.

Or “heads of grain.” While the generic term στάχυς (stachus) can refer to the cluster of seeds at the top of grain such as barley or wheat, in the NT the term is restricted to wheat (L&N 3.40; BDAG 941 s.v. 1). KJV “corn” is the result of British English, in which “corn” refers to the main cereal crop of a district, wheat in England and oats in Scotland (British English uses “maize” to refer to American corn).

verses.zh: 法利赛人看见，就对耶稣说：「看哪，你的门徒做安息日不可做的事了！」
verses.en: But when the Pharisees[NOTE:1] saw this they said to him, “Look, your disciples are doing what is against the law to do on the Sabbath.”
notes: See the note on Pharisees in 3:7.

verses.zh: 耶稣对他们说：「经上记着大卫和跟从他的人饥饿之时所做的事，你们没有念过吗？
verses.en: He[NOTE:1] said to them, “Haven’t you read what David did when he and his companions were hungry—
notes: Here δέ (de) has not been translated.

verses.zh: 他怎么进了　神的殿，吃了陈设饼，这饼不是他和跟从他的人可以吃得，惟独祭司才可以吃。
verses.en: how he entered the house of God and ate[NOTE:1] the sacred bread,[NOTE:2] which was against the law[NOTE:3] for him or his companions to eat, but only for the priests?[NOTE:4]
notes: ‡ The Greek verb ἔφαγεν (ephagen, “he ate”) is found in a majority of witnesses across a broad geogrphical area (P70 C D L N W Γ Δ Θ ƒ1, 13 33 565 579 700 1424 M latt sy co; SBL). NA28 has the plural ἔφαγον (ephagon, “they ate”), the wording found in א B 481. Although it is quite possible that ἔφαγεν was motivated by the parallels in Mark and Luke, both of which have the singular, the minimal—though early and significant—attestation for the plural, coupled with the singular being a more difficult reading (since the context implies that David’s companions also ate), gives the edge to ἔφαγεν as the likely autographic wording.

Grk “the bread of presentation.” sn The sacred bread refers to the “bread of presentation,” “showbread,” or “bread of the Presence,” twelve loaves prepared weekly for the tabernacle and later, the temple. See Exod 25:30; 35:13; 39:36; Lev 24:5-9. Each loaf was made from 3 quarts (3.5 liters; Heb “two-tenths of an ephah”) of fine flour. The loaves were placed on a table in the holy place of the tabernacle, on the north side opposite the lampstand (Exod 26:35). It was the duty of the priest each Sabbath to place fresh bread on the table; the loaves from the previous week were then given to Aaron and his descendants, who ate them in the holy place because they were considered sacred (Lev 24:9). See also Mark 2:23-28, Luke 6:1-5.

Jesus’ response to the charge that what his disciples were doing was against the law is one of analogy: “If David did it for his troops in a time of need, then so can I with my disciples.” Jesus is clear that on the surface there was a violation here. What is not as clear is whether he is arguing a “greater need” makes this permissible or that this was within the intention of the law all along.
See 1 Sam 21:1-6.

verses.zh: 再者，律法上所记的，当安息日，祭司在殿里犯了安息日还是没有罪，你们没有念过吗？
verses.en: Or have you not read in the law that the priests in the temple desecrate the Sabbath and yet are not guilty?

verses.zh: 但我告诉你们，在这里有一人比殿更大。
verses.en: I[NOTE:1] tell you that something greater than the temple is here.
notes: Here δέ (de) has not been translated.

verses.zh: 『我喜爱怜恤，不喜爱祭祀。』你们若明白这话的意思，就不将无罪的当作有罪的了。
verses.en: If[NOTE:1] you had known what this means: ‘I want mercy and not sacrifice,’[NOTE:2] you would not have condemned the innocent.
notes: Here δέ (de) has not been translated.
A quotation from Hos 6:6 (see also Matt 9:13).

verses.zh: 因为人子是安息日的主。」
verses.en: For the Son of Man is lord[NOTE:1] of the Sabbath.”
notes: The term “lord” is in emphatic position in the Greek text.sn A second point in Jesus’ defense of his disciples’ actions was that his authority as Son of Man also allowed it, since as Son of Man he was lord of the Sabbath.

verses.zh: 耶稣离开那地方，进了一个会堂。
verses.en: Then[NOTE:1] Jesus[NOTE:2] left that place and entered their synagogue.[NOTE:3]
notes: Here καί (kai) has been translated as “then” to indicate the implied sequence of events within the narrative.
Grk “he”; the referent (Jesus) has been specified in the translation for clarity.
See the note on synagogues in 4:23.

verses.zh: 那里有一个人枯干了一只手。有人问耶稣说：「安息日治病可以不可以？」意思是要控告他。
verses.en: A[NOTE:1] man was there who had a withered[NOTE:2] hand. And they asked Jesus,[NOTE:3] “Is it lawful to heal on the Sabbath?”[NOTE:4] so that they could accuse him.
notes: Grk “And behold.” The Greek word ἰδού (idou) has not been translated because it has no exact English equivalent here, but adds interest and emphasis (BDAG 468 s.v. 1).
Withered means the man’s hand was shrunken and paralyzed.
Grk “and they asked him, saying.” The participle λέγοντες (legontes) is redundant and has not been translated. The referent of the pronoun (Jesus) has been specified in the translation for clarity.
The background for this is the view that only if life was endangered should one attempt to heal on the Sabbath (see the Mishnah, m. Shabbat 6.3; 12.1; 18.3; 19.2; m. Yoma 8.6).

verses.zh: 耶稣说：「你们中间谁有一只羊，当安息日掉在坑里，不把它抓住，拉上来呢？
verses.en: He said to them, “Would not any one of you, if he had one sheep that fell into a pit on the Sabbath, take hold of it and lift it out?

verses.zh: 人比羊何等贵重呢！所以，在安息日做善事是可以的。」
verses.en: How much more valuable is a person than a sheep! So it is lawful to do good on the Sabbath.”

verses.zh: 于是对那人说：「伸出手来！」他把手一伸，手就复了原，和那只手一样。
verses.en: Then he said to the man, “Stretch out your hand.” He stretched it out and it was restored,[NOTE:1] as healthy as the other.
notes: The passive was restored points to healing by God. Now the question became: Would God exercise his power through Jesus, if what Jesus was doing were wrong? Note also Jesus’ “labor.” He simply spoke and it was so.

verses.zh: 法利赛人出去，商议怎样可以除灭耶稣。
verses.en: But the Pharisees went out and plotted against him, as to how they could assassinate[NOTE:1] him.
notes: Grk “destroy.”

verses.zh: 耶稣知道了，就离开那里，有许多人跟着他。他把其中有病的人都治好了；
verses.en: Now when Jesus learned of this, he went away from there. Great[NOTE:1] crowds[NOTE:2] followed him, and he healed them all.
notes: Here καί (kai) has not been translated.

א B lat read only πολλοί (polloi, “many”) here, the first hand of N reads ὄχλοι (ochloi, “crowds”), while virtually all the rest of the witnesses have ὄχλοι πολλοί (ochloi polloi, “great crowds”). In spite of the good quality of both א and B (especially in combination), and the testimony of the Latin witnesses, the longer reading is most likely correct; the shorter readings were likely due to homoioteleuton. NA28 puts ὄχλοι in brackets, indicating the difficulty in choosing on reading over the other.

verses.zh: 又嘱咐他们，不要给他传名。
verses.en: But he sternly warned them not to make him known.

verses.zh: 这是要应验先知以赛亚的话，说：
verses.en: This fulfilled what was spoken by the prophet Isaiah:[NOTE:1]
notes: Grk “so that what was said by Isaiah the prophet would be fulfilled, saying.” This final clause, however, is part of one sentence in Greek (vv. 15b-17) and is thus not related only to v. 16. The participle λέγοντος (legontos) is redundant and has not been translated.

verses.zh: 看哪！我的仆人，我所拣选、所亲爱、心里所喜悦的，我要将我的灵赐给他；他必将公理传给外邦。
verses.en: “Here is[NOTE:1] my servant whom I have chosen, the one I love, in whom I take great delight.[NOTE:2] I will put my Spirit on him, and he will proclaim justice to the nations.
notes: Grk “Behold my servant.”
Grk “in whom my soul is well pleased.”

verses.zh: 他不争竞，不喧嚷；街上也没有人听见他的声音。
verses.en: He will not quarrel or cry out, nor will anyone hear his voice in the streets.

verses.zh: 压伤的芦苇，他不折断；将残的灯火，他不吹灭；等他施行公理，叫公理得胜。
verses.en: He will not break a bruised reed or extinguish a smoldering wick, until he brings justice to victory.

verses.zh: 外邦人都要仰望他的名。
verses.en: And in his name the Gentiles[NOTE:1] will hope.”[NOTE:2]
notes: Or “the nations” (the same Greek word may be translated “Gentiles” or “nations”).
Verses 18-21 are a quotation from Isa 42:1-4.

verses.zh: 当下，有人将一个被鬼附着、又瞎又哑的人带到耶稣那里，耶稣就医治他，甚至那哑巴又能说话，又能看见。
verses.en: Then they brought to him a demon-possessed man who was blind and mute. Jesus[NOTE:1] healed him so that he could speak and see.[NOTE:2]
notes: Grk “And he”; the referent (Jesus) has been specified in the translation for clarity.
Grk “so that the mute man spoke and saw.”

verses.zh: 众人都惊奇，说：「这不是大卫的子孙吗？」
verses.en: All the crowds were amazed and said, “Could this one be the Son of David?”

verses.zh: 但法利赛人听见，就说：「这个人赶鬼，无非是靠着鬼王别西卜啊。」
verses.en: But when the Pharisees[NOTE:1] heard this they said, “He does not cast out demons except by the power of Beelzebul,[NOTE:2] the ruler[NOTE:3] of demons!”
notes: See the note on Pharisees in 3:7.
Grk “except by Beelzebul.”sn Beelzebul is another name for Satan. So some people recognized Jesus’ work as supernatural, but called it diabolical.
Or “prince.”

verses.zh: 耶稣知道他们的意念，就对他们说：「凡一国自相纷争，就成为荒场；一城一家自相纷争，必站立不住；
verses.en: Now when Jesus[NOTE:1] realized what they were thinking, he said to them,[NOTE:2] “Every kingdom divided against itself is destroyed,[NOTE:3] and no town or house divided against itself will stand.
notes: The majority of mss read ὁ ᾿Ιησοῦς (ho Iēsous, “Jesus”), which clarifies who is the subject of the sentence. Although the shorter text is attested in far fewer witnesses (P21 א B D 892* sys,c sa bo), both the pedigree of the mss and the strong internal evidence (viz., scribes were not prone to intentionally delete the name of Jesus) argue for the omission of Jesus’ name. The name has been included in the translation, however, for clarity.

Jesus here demonstrated the absurdity of the thinking of the religious leaders who maintained that he was in league with Satan and that he actually derived his power from the devil. He first teaches (vv. 25-28) that if he casts out demons by the ruler of the demons, then in reality Satan is fighting against himself, with the result that his kingdom has come to an end. He then teaches (v. 29) about tying up the strong man to prove that he does not need to align himself with the devil because he is more powerful. Jesus defeated Satan at his temptation (4:1-11) and by his exorcisms he clearly demonstrated himself to be stronger than the devil. The passage reveals the desperate condition of the religious leaders, who in their hatred for Jesus end up attributing the work of the Holy Spirit to Satan (a position for which they will be held accountable, 12:31-32).
Or “is left in ruins.”

verses.zh: 若撒但赶逐撒但，就是自相纷争，他的国怎能站得住呢？
verses.en: So if[NOTE:1] Satan casts out Satan, he is divided against himself. How then will his kingdom stand?
notes: This first class condition, the first of three “if” clauses in the following verses, presents the example vividly as if it were so. In fact, all three conditions in these verses are first class. The examples are made totally parallel. The expected answer is that Satan’s kingdom will not stand, so the suggestion makes no sense. Satan would not seek to heal.

verses.zh: 我若靠着别西卜赶鬼，你们的子弟赶鬼又靠着谁呢？这样，他们就要断定你们的是非。
verses.en: And if I cast out demons by Beelzebul, by whom do your sons[NOTE:1] cast them[NOTE:2] out? For this reason they will be your judges.
notes: Most read your sons as a reference to Jewish exorcists (cf. “your followers,” L&N 9.4), but more likely this is a reference to the disciples of Jesus themselves, who are also Jewish and have been healing as well (R. J. Shirock, “Whose Exorcists are they? The Referents of οἱ υἱοὶ ὑμῶν at Matthew 12:27/Luke 11:19, ” JSNT 46 [1992]: 41-51). If this is a reference to the disciples, then Jesus’ point is that it is not only him, but those associated with him whose power the hearers must assess. The following reference to judging also favors this reading.
The pronoun “them” is not in the Greek text, but is implied. Direct objects were frequently omitted in Greek when clear from the context.

verses.zh: 我若靠着　神的灵赶鬼，这就是　神的国临到你们了。
verses.en: But if I cast out demons by the Spirit of God, then the kingdom of God[NOTE:1] has already overtaken[NOTE:2] you.
notes: God’s kingdom is a major theme of Jesus’ teaching. The nature of the kingdom of God in the NT and in Jesus’ teaching has long been debated by interpreters and scholars, with discussion primarily centering around the nature of the kingdom (earthly, heavenly, or both) and the kingdom’s arrival (present, future, or both). An additional major issue concerns the relationship between the kingdom of God and the person and work of Jesus himself.

The phrase ἔφθασεν ἐφ᾿ ὑμᾶς (ephthasen eph’ humas) is quite important. Does it mean merely “approach” (which would be reflected in a translation like “has come near to you”) or actually “come upon” (as in the translation given above, “has already overtaken you,” which has the added connotation of suddenness)? Is the arrival of the kingdom merely anticipated or already in process? Two factors favor arrival over anticipation here. First, the accusative case prepositional phrase ἐφ᾿ ὑμᾶς (eph’ humas, “upon you”) in the Greek text in combination with this verb suggests arrival (Dan 4:24, 28 Theodotion). Second, the following illustration in v. 29 looks at the healing as portraying Satan being overrun. So the presence of God’s authority has arrived. See also L&N 13.123 for the translation of φθάνω (phthanō) as “to happen to already, to come upon, to come upon already.”

verses.zh: 人怎能进壮士家里，抢夺他的家具呢？除非先捆住那壮士，才可以抢夺他的家财。
verses.en: How[NOTE:1] else can someone enter a strong man’s[NOTE:2] house and steal his property, unless he first ties up the strong man? Then he can thoroughly plunder the house.[NOTE:3]
notes: Grk “Or how can.”
The strong man here pictures Satan.

Some see the imagery here as similar to Eph 4:7-10, although no opponents are explicitly named in that passage. Jesus has the victory over Satan. Jesus’ acts of healing mean that the war is being won and the kingdom is coming.

verses.zh: 不与我相合的，就是敌我的；不同我收聚的，就是分散的。」
verses.en: Whoever is not with me is against me,[NOTE:1] and whoever does not gather with me scatters.[NOTE:2]
notes: Whoever is not with me is against me. The call here is to join the victor. Failure to do so means that one is being destructive. Responding to Jesus is the issue.
For the image of scattering, see Pss. Sol. 17:18.

verses.zh: 所以我告诉你们：「人一切的罪和亵渎的话都可得赦免，惟独亵渎圣灵，总不得赦免。
verses.en: For this reason I tell you, people will be forgiven for every sin and blasphemy,[NOTE:1] but the blasphemy against the Spirit will not be forgiven.
notes: Grk “every sin and blasphemy will be forgiven men.”

verses.zh: 凡说话干犯人子的，还可得赦免；惟独说话干犯圣灵的，今世来世总不得赦免。」
verses.en: Whoever speaks a word against the Son of Man will be forgiven.[NOTE:1] But whoever speaks against the Holy Spirit will not be forgiven,[NOTE:2] either in this age or in the age to come.
notes: Grk “it will be forgiven him.”

Grk “it will not be forgiven him.”sn Whoever speaks against the Holy Spirit will not be forgiven. This passage has troubled many people, who have wondered whether or not they have committed this sin. Three things must be kept in mind: (1) the nature of the sin is to ascribe what is the obvious work of the Holy Spirit (e.g., releasing people from Satan’s power) to Satan himself; (2) it is not simply a momentary doubt or sinful attitude, but is indeed a settled condition which opposes the Spirit’s work, as typified by the religious leaders who opposed Jesus; and (3) a person who is concerned about it has probably never committed this sin, for those who commit it here (i.e., the religious leaders) are not in the least concerned about Jesus’ warning.

verses.zh: 「你们或以为树好，果子也好；树坏，果子也坏；因为看果子就可以知道树。
verses.en: “Make a tree good and its fruit will be good, or make a tree bad[NOTE:1] and its fruit will be bad, for a tree is known by its fruit.
notes: Grk “rotten.” The word σαπρός, modifying both “tree” and “fruit,” can also mean “diseased” (L&N 65.28).

verses.zh: 毒蛇的种类！你们既是恶人，怎能说出好话来呢？因为心里所充满的，口里就说出来。
verses.en: Offspring of vipers! How are you able to say anything good, since you are evil? For the mouth speaks from what fills the heart.

verses.zh: 善人从他心里所存的善就发出善来；恶人从他心里所存的恶就发出恶来。
verses.en: The good person[NOTE:1] brings good things out of his[NOTE:2] good treasury,[NOTE:3] and the evil person brings evil things out of his evil treasury.
notes: The Greek text reads here ἄνθρωπος (anthrōpos). The term is generic referring to any person.
Grk “the”; the Greek article has been translated here and in the following clause (“his evil treasury”) as a possessive pronoun (ExSyn 215).
The treasury here is a metaphorical reference to a person’s heart (cf. BDAG 456 s.v. θησαυρός 1.b and the parallel passage in Luke 6:45).

verses.zh: 我又告诉你们，凡人所说的闲话，当审判的日子，必要句句供出来；
verses.en: I[NOTE:1] tell you that on the day of judgment, people will give an account for every worthless word they speak.
notes: Here δέ (de) has not been translated.

verses.zh: 因为要凭你的话定你为义，也要凭你的话定你有罪。」
verses.en: For by your words you will be justified, and by your words you will be condemned.”

verses.zh: 当时，有几个文士和法利赛人对耶稣说：「夫子，我们愿意你显个神迹给我们看。」
verses.en: Then some of the experts in the law[NOTE:1] along with some Pharisees[NOTE:2] answered him,[NOTE:3] “Teacher, we want to see a sign[NOTE:4] from you.”
notes: Or “Then some of the scribes.” See the note on the phrase “experts in the law” in 2:4.
See the note on Pharisees in 3:7.tn Grk “and Pharisees.” The word “some” before “Pharisees” has been supplied for clarification.
Grk “answered him, saying.” The participle λέγοντες (legontes) is redundant, but the syntax of the sentence was changed to conform to English style.
What exactly this sign would have been, given what Jesus was already doing, is not clear. But here is where the fence-sitters reside, refusing to commit to him.

verses.zh: 耶稣回答说：「一个邪恶淫乱的世代求看神迹，除了先知约拿的神迹以外，再没有神迹给他们看。
verses.en: But he answered them,[NOTE:1] “An evil and adulterous generation asks for a sign, but no sign will be given to it except the sign of the prophet Jonah.
notes: Grk “But answering, he said to them.” This construction is somewhat redundant in English and has been simplified in the translation.

verses.zh: 约拿三日三夜在大鱼肚腹中，人子也要这样三日三夜在地里头。
verses.en: For just as Jonah was in the belly of the huge fish[NOTE:1] for three days and three nights,[NOTE:2] so the Son of Man will be in the heart of the earth for three days and three nights.
notes: Grk “large sea creature.”
A quotation from Jonah 1:17.

verses.zh: 当审判的时候，尼尼微人要起来定这世代的罪，因为尼尼微人听了约拿所传的就悔改了。看哪，在这里有一人比约拿更大！
verses.en: The people[NOTE:1] of Nineveh will stand up at the judgment with this generation and condemn it because they repented when Jonah preached to them[NOTE:2]—and now,[NOTE:3] something greater than Jonah is here!
notes: Grk “men”; the word here (ἀνήρ, anēr) usually indicates males or husbands, but occasionally is used in a generic sense of people in general, as here (cf. BDAG 79 s.v. 1.a, 2).
Grk “at the preaching of Jonah.”
Grk “behold.”

verses.zh: 当审判的时候，南方的女王要起来定这世代的罪，因为她从地极而来，要听所罗门的智慧话。看哪，在这里有一人比所罗门更大。」
verses.en: The queen of the South[NOTE:1] will rise up at the judgment with this generation and condemn it because she came from the ends of the earth to hear the wisdom of Solomon—and now,[NOTE:2] something greater than Solomon is here!
notes: On the queen of the South see 1 Kgs 10:1-3 and 2 Chr 9:1-12, as well as Josephus, Ant. 8.6.5-6 (8.165-175). The South most likely refers to modern southwest Arabia, possibly the eastern part of modern Yemen, although there is an ancient tradition reflected in Josephus which identifies this geo-political entity as Ethiopia.
Grk “behold.”

verses.zh: 「污鬼离了人身，就在无水之地过来过去，寻求安歇之处，却寻不着。
verses.en: “When[NOTE:1] an unclean spirit[NOTE:2] goes out of a person,[NOTE:3] it passes through waterless places[NOTE:4] looking for rest but[NOTE:5] does not find it.
notes: Here δέ (de) has not been translated.
Unclean spirit refers to an evil spirit.
Grk “man.” This is a generic use of ἄνθρωπος (anthrōpos), referring to both males and females. This same use occurs in v. 45.

The background for the reference to waterless places is not entirely clear, though some Jewish texts suggest spirits must have a place to dwell, but not with water (Luke 8:29-31; Tob 8:3). Some suggest that the image of the desert or deserted cities as the places demons dwell is where this idea started (Isa 13:21; 34:14).
Here καί (kai) has been translated as “but” to indicate the contrast present in this context.

verses.zh: 于是说：『我要回到我所出来的屋里去。』到了，就看见里面空闲，打扫干净，修饰好了，
verses.en: Then it says, ‘I will return to the home I left.’[NOTE:1] When it returns,[NOTE:2] it finds the house[NOTE:3] empty, swept clean, and put in order.[NOTE:4]
notes: Grk “I will return to my house from which I came.”
Grk “comes.”
The words “the house” are not in Greek but are implied.

The image of the house empty, swept clean, and put in order refers to the life of the person from whom the demon departed. The key to the example appears to be that no one else has been invited in to dwell. If an exorcism occurs and there is no response to God, then the way is free for the demon to return. Some see the reference to exorcism as more symbolic; thus the story’s only point is about responding to Jesus. This is possible and certainly is an application of the passage.

verses.zh: 便去另带了七个比自己更恶的鬼来，都进去住在那里。那人末后的景况比先前更不好了。这邪恶的世代也要如此。」
verses.en: Then it goes and brings with it seven other spirits more evil than itself, and they go in and live there, so[NOTE:1] the last state of that person is worse than the first. It will be that way for this evil generation as well!”
notes: Here καί (kai) has been translated as “so” to indicate the concluding point of the story.

verses.zh: 耶稣还对众人说话的时候，不料他母亲和他弟兄站在外边，要与他说话。
verses.en: While Jesus[NOTE:1] was still speaking to the crowds,[NOTE:2] his mother and brothers[NOTE:3] came and stood outside, asking[NOTE:4] to speak to him.
notes: Grk “he”; the referent (Jesus) has been specified in the translation for clarity.
Grk “crowds, behold, his mother.” The Greek word ἰδού (idou) has not been translated because it has no exact English equivalent here, but adds interest and emphasis (BDAG 468 s.v. 1).

The issue of whether Jesus had brothers (siblings) has had a long history in the church. Epiphanius, in the 4th century, argued that Mary was a perpetual virgin and had no offspring other than Jesus. Others argued that these brothers were really cousins. Nothing in the text suggests any of this. See also John 7:3.
Grk “seeking.”

verses.zh: 有人告诉他说：「看哪，你母亲和你弟兄站在外边，要与你说话。」
verses.en: [NOTE:1] Someone[NOTE:2] told him, “Look, your mother and your brothers are standing outside wanting[NOTE:3] to speak to you.”
notes: A few ancient mss and versions lack this verse (א* B L Γ ff1 k sys,c sa), while almost all the rest have it. The witness of א and B is especially strong, but internal considerations override this external evidence. Both v. 46 and v. 47 end with the word λαλῆσαι (“to speak”), so early scribes probably omitted the verse through homoioteleuton. Without v. 47 the passage is nonsensical: v. 46 says Jesus’ family members wanted to speak to him, and v. 48 begins with “to the one who said this.” The antecedent of “the one who said this” must surely be “someone” in v. 47. Thus, the omission of v. 47 is too hard a reading. This verse therefore should be regarded as part of the Ausgangstext.
Here δέ (de) has not been translated.
Grk “seeking.”

verses.zh: 他却回答那人说：「谁是我的母亲？谁是我的弟兄？」
verses.en: To the one who had said this, Jesus[NOTE:1] replied,[NOTE:2] “Who is my mother and who are my brothers?”
notes: Grk “he”; the referent (Jesus) has been specified in the translation for clarity.

Grk “And answering, he said to the one who had said this.” This construction is somewhat redundant in English and has been simplified in the translation. Here δέ (de) at the beginning of the clause has not been translated.

verses.zh: 就伸手指着门徒，说：「看哪，我的母亲，我的弟兄。
verses.en: And pointing[NOTE:1] toward his disciples he said, “Here[NOTE:2] are my mother and my brothers!
notes: Grk “extending his hand.”
Grk “Behold my mother and my brothers.”

verses.zh: 凡遵行我天父旨意的人，就是我的弟兄姊妹和母亲了。」
verses.en: For whoever does the will of my Father in heaven is[NOTE:1] my brother and sister and mother.”
notes: The pleonastic pronoun αὐτός (autos, “he”) which precedes this verb has not been translated.
